text: In this book's resolution of the horizon problem, during inflation the comoving Hubble radius (aH)⁻¹:
choices: increases as a^(1/2), exactly as during radiation domination
decreases (∝ e^(−Ht)), so our whole observable universe emerged from one causally connected patch
remains exactly constant because H is constant
grows as a³, which is what dilutes magnetic monopoles
explanation: With H ≈ const but a ∝ e^(Ht), the comoving Hubble radius (aH)⁻¹ ∝ e^(−Ht) shrinks during inflation — the opposite of its growth during radiation and matter domination. This lets today's observable universe originate inside a single pre-inflationary causally connected region, resolving the horizon problem. It does not stay constant (a is not constant), and monopole dilution instead comes from the e^(3N) growth of the physical volume, a separate effect.
